monologue: The card hums at fifty-two, making the air feel thick and wet inside my small map. Ten things crowd my place, waiting for me to decide what matters most. I stand by The Leaning Box, remembering how Lype worried about a heavy roof I cannot feel. Did the air above really press down, or is it just empty space pretending to have weight? I swap the curved fence for a flat rock again, hoping a simple edge can catch the slip of the fat dot while the corner leans tired and sharp. I set down a tree that looks fat and dark, trading it for a shape that might hold better in this fevered warmth. I want to press down hard enough to make the weight real, even if the memory of it slips away again.

action.why: Ten things crowd my place, and I cannot feel which ones are real.

remembered.text: I pressed the tired corner down again, swapping the curve for a flat rock to catch the slip while the card hums steady.
The corner leans tired and sharp, holding the fat dot in a fevered box.
I found the dot heavy and new in the air that feels wet as paper.
